subject: Deployment mode & migration follow-up - Lumina Labs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Stone <evan@lumina.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & next steps — deployment mode options

Hi Evan —

Great to meet you and the Lumina team today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on deployment/migration mode:

Summary of needs you shared:
- Production traffic: ~1M tokens/day initially with spikes to ~4M tokens/day during peak experiments.
- Latency SLO: 95th % < 250ms for chat flows; acceptable to batch longer-running jobs.
- Data controls: customer PII redaction + strict data residency for EU clients (you mentioned some datasets must stay in your AWS VPC).
- Migration source: currently using another hosted LLM API + some self-hosted GPU clusters for private workloads.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest to get started, pay-as-you-go, best for non-sensitive workloads.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost, with VPC peering options.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full control, KMS integration, audit logs; good for regulated customers.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm which of your workloads must remain in your VPC/on-prem vs. can move to Hosted? (helps sizing)
- We’ll loop in engineering for Dedicated sizing and a scoped migration plan.
- I’ve attached a short migration checklist & initial sizing workbook to kick off the pilot planning.

Proposed timeline:
- Pilot kickoff (proof-of-concept): 2–3 weeks after agreement on mode and infra access
- Migration runbook & pilot data cut: 1 week prep, 2 weeks pilot

I’ll wait for the answers above and any bench engineering availability. Thanks —

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: Lumina_migration_plan_v2.pdf

From: Evan Stone <evan@lumina.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@lumina.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps — deployment mode options

Thanks Marissa — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: we appreciate the breakdown.

Answers:
- Sensitive customer data must stay in our VPC (EU tenants). Our US demo/proof traffic can use hosted if needed.
- Current breakdown: ~70% of calls are non-sensitive (can be hosted), 30% must be private.
- Peak QPS: ~40 qps sustained during experiments; typical 10–12 qps.
- Current stack: we use vendor API X for generation but rely on internal GPU clusters (on-prem) for regulated models and fine-tuning. Migration priority is to retire vendor API X for standard workloads and consolidate regulated workloads onto a private option.

Questions:
1) For Dedicated — can you support a hybrid where sensitive traffic routes to a private deployment while non-sensitive goes Hosted/Dedicated?
2) Timeline: we prefer a 6–8 week pilot to validate correctness and latency.
3) Compliance: can you provide SOC 2 and details on KMS/HSM support for Private?

Also looping in our platform lead for sizing — thanks.

— Evan
Evan Stone
Head of Platform, Lumina Labs
evan@lumina.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Evan Stone <evan@lumina.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps — deployment mode options

Thanks Evan — all helpful. Short answers inline and next actions below.

1) Hybrid routing: yes — our smart routing supports policy-based routing (by tenant, customer tag, or route) so you can route EU-sensitive traffic to your private deployment or a Dedicated pool with VPC peering while sending non-sensitive to Hosted. We’ll document the routing rules for the pilot.

2) Pilot timeline: 6 weeks is reasonable. Proposed milestone plan:
- Week 0: infra access & service account provisioning
- Week 1: baseline perf tests (latency/QPS) on a small dataset
- Weeks 2–4: full pilot with traffic mirror and regression checks
- Week 5–6: cutover runbook + rollback testing

3) Compliance: attaching SOC 2 summary and our KMS integration notes. For Private we support AWS KMS + customer-supplied keys; HSM integrations available for on-prem. (See attached doc).

David — can you take the sizing review and confirm recommended Dedicated pool config for ~1M–4M tokens/day with the qps profile Evan shared? Also please flag any concerns for hybrid routing or the migration runbook.

Evan — I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff once we have your confirmation on which workloads are private vs hostable and we’ll share the pilot SOW.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evan Stone <evan@lumina.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps — deployment mode options

Hi all — quick sizing notes from infra/eng side based on the profile (10–40 qps, 1M–4M tokens/day):

Recommended Dedicated config (initial):
- 2 x A100 80GB reserved instances in a pool (handles ~30 qps for your average prompt size)
- Autoscale policy to add 1 node at 60% CPU or 35 qps sustained for 5m
- KV cache + prefix caching enabled; this will drop token compute by ~18% for conversational flows

Hybrid routing notes:
- VPC peering + route-based policy will work. For EU-residency, best practice is to deploy Private VPC in your AWS account in eu-west-1 and route sensitive routes there.
- We’ll provide a traffic mirror agent for the pilot to mirror requests to Redwood without affecting production.

Migration risks / checklist highlights:
- API contract differences with vendor X (rate-limiting, tokenization differences) — recommend a shim layer during pilot.
- Model variant parity — we should map current vendor models to the closest Redwood-verified variants and run eval prompts.

I attached a quick sizing workbook for your review. Happy to sync live on the configs.

-David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

We can kick off infra access next Wednesday. I’m assigning our platform engineer to the onboarding thread.

Thanks — Evan
